hypotheticals.question: Whether BNS s. 108 (Abetment of suicide) applies, and how structured written arguments should be framed.
hypotheticals.analysis:
Step 1 — Identify the provision. The correct current-law cite is BNS s. 108 (Abetment of suicide), Chapter VI — Of Offences Affecting the Human Body.
Step 2 — State the legal test in your own words, then list the ingredients:
   (1) If any person commits suicide, whoever abets the commission of such suicide, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine
Step 3 — Check limitations, provisos and the rest of the Chapter so you do not apply s. 108 in a vacuum.
Step 4 — Map each fact to an ingredient. Write “this fact proves ingredient (a)” or “this fact is missing, so the section is not made out”.
Step 5 — Conclude. If every essential ingredient is proved and no exception covers the case, BNS s. 108 applies. If any essential ingredient fails, say so and stop. Do not invent a different section to save the answer.

questionsAndAnswers.question: Legal Assessment & Statutory Note: BNS s. 108 (Abetment of suicide)
questionsAndAnswers.answer:
Introduction. BNS s. 108 deals with Abetment of suicide. It sits in Chapter VI — Of Offences Affecting the Human Body of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023. After 1 July 2024 this is the current-law citation for this offence / definition / punishment.

Meaning. Abetment of suicide (old 306). The person who dies is not the accused. Instigation, conspiracy or aid (s. 45) plus a suicide is the structure. Leave-note cases still turn on whether there was instigation, not mere harassment.

Legal rule. In student language: BNS s. 108 is the rule on “Abetment of suicide”. The section provides that if any person commits suicide, whoever abets the commission of such suicide, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine. Do not stop at the heading. An examiner awards marks for the ingredients, the explanations and the illustrations, not for writing the title alone.

Essential ingredients. An authoritative analysis must list them, not hide them in one paragraph:
1. If any person commits suicide, whoever abets the commission of such suicide, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine

Illustration. Give one short original example (label it as an example) and apply the ingredients.

Limitations. Apply only the conditions written in s. 108. Do not import a defence from a different chapter unless the question requires it.

Connected sections. Read with BNS s. 107, BNS s. 45, BNS s. 226. A preliminary brief mentions the neighbour; comprehensive submissions explain the exact distinction.

Conclusion. BNS s. 108 is the complete current-law heading for Abetment of suicide. Define, list ingredients, use an illustration, note any explanation or exception, apply, cite. That is a complete statutory structure.

Comprehensive Written Submissions. Deepen the doctrinal synthesis with four foundational layers.

Layer 1 — Place the section in the Chapter. Homicide, organised crime, terrorism, hurt, acid, restraint, assault, kidnapping and trafficking.. Show why this heading sits where it sits.

Layer 2 — Work a second, slightly harder hypothetical. Change one ingredient and show why the section then fails.

Layer 3 — Distinction. Contrast BNS s. 108 with BNS s. 107, BNS s. 45, BNS s. 226. Write a short table in prose: meaning, ingredients, stage of the case, consequence. Confusion of neighbouring sections is the most common reason arguments collapse under judicial scrutiny.



Layer 5 — Application and current-law close. Apply the test to the problem facts in IRAC form (Issue, Rule, Application, Conclusion). Close with: “The governing citation on or after 1 July 2024 is BNS s. 108.”

learningObjectives: Explain the statutory structure of abetment of suicide under BNS s. 108.
Distinguish abetment from mere harassment or disagreement by identifying the required mental and causal links.
Apply the rule to a problem question using an ingredient-by-ingredient method.
Construct short, 10-mark and 16-mark examination answers without replacing the migrated study material.
enhancement.definition: BNS s. 108 creates the punishment provision for abetment of suicide. The offence must be read with the statutory concept of abetment in BNS s. 45; the student should therefore identify the particular form of abetment alleged rather than treating every unpleasant act as instigation.
enhancement.legalPrinciple: The central exam issue is whether the accused's conduct legally amounts to abetment and has the required connection with the suicide. Supreme Court decisions on the predecessor IPC provisions emphasise that a prosecution must identify instigation, conspiracy or intentional aid and establish the necessary nexus rather than rely on the fact of suicide alone.
statutoryFramework: Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 — s. 108 (abetment of suicide)
Use the BNS text for the current statutory wording; older IPC s. 107/s. 306 authorities are historical precedents and must be identified as such.
essentialIngredients: A person must have committed suicide.
The accused must have abetted that suicide within the statutory forms of abetment.
Where instigation is alleged, the facts must support the required incitement or encouragement and the legally relevant connection to the suicide.
The prosecution must prove the required mental element and causal connection from the evidence; the occurrence of suicide by itself is not enough.
enhancement.detailedExplanation: For an exam answer, begin with the statutory scheme rather than a case name. Read s. 108 together with s. 45. Then separate the factual questions: what exactly did the accused do, which form of abetment is alleged, what evidence proves that conduct, and how does the conduct connect to the suicide? Supreme Court authority under the predecessor provisions is useful for explaining the doctrinal test, but the current citation should remain BNS s. 108. A strong answer also distinguishes a direct act of instigation from conduct that is merely harsh, unpleasant or morally blameworthy. The question is whether the legal ingredients are proved, not whether the accused behaved badly in the abstract.
examples: Example — direct instigation: A repeatedly and deliberately urges B to end his life, in circumstances from which the required intention and connection can be proved, and B thereafter commits suicide. The answer should identify the alleged instigation, evidence and proximity rather than simply state that A caused B's death.

Example — insufficient reasoning: A and B have an argument and B later dies by suicide. The fact of the argument alone does not establish every ingredient of abetment. The answer must identify evidence of instigation, intentional aid or conspiracy and the required nexus.
distinctions: Abetment of suicide vs. mere harassment: harassment may be relevant evidence, but the statutory ingredients of abetment must still be proved.
Current BNS citation vs. historical IPC citation: BNS s. 108 is the current provision; IPC s. 306 may appear in older judgments and should be labelled as historical correspondence.
Instigation vs. intentional aid: identify the actual form of abetment alleged and prove its ingredients instead of using the terms interchangeably.
caseLaw: M. Mohan v. State, (2011) 3 SCC 626 — Supreme Court authority frequently cited for the requirement of a positive act and the mental element in abetment of suicide under the predecessor IPC provisions.
Amalendu Pal alias Jhantu v. State of West Bengal, (2010) 1 SCC 707 — predecessor-IPC authority relevant to the requirement that the conduct amount to abetment rather than mere harassment.

Supreme Court, Criminal Appeal arising from SLP (Crl.) No. 14640 of 2025, judgment dated 16 April 2026 — recent Supreme Court discussion reiterating that instigation/incitement is central and that the required connection between the conduct and suicide must be established.
problemApplication: Issue: identify whether the accused's proved conduct falls within a statutory form of abetment.
Rule: read BNS ss. 45 and 108 together and use predecessor-case authorities only for the doctrinal principle they actually establish.
Application: map each material fact to the alleged instigation, conspiracy or intentional aid; separately analyse intention, evidence and temporal/causal connection.
Counterpoint: do not convert every quarrel, criticism or workplace/family dispute into abetment without identifying the statutory ingredient supported by evidence.
Conclusion: state whether each essential ingredient is proved, not merely whether the accused's conduct appears blameworthy.

shortAnswer: Define s. 108 and link it to s. 45.
State that the fact of suicide alone is insufficient.
Conclude with the current BNS citation.
tenMark: One leading Supreme Court authority and its principle.
sixteenMark: Detailed explanation of each form of abetment relevant to the problem.
Two or more verified authorities, clearly identified as predecessor-IPC precedents where applicable.

keyTakeaways: Suicide alone does not prove abetment.
Identify the precise alleged act of instigation, conspiracy or intentional aid.
Use older IPC judgments as historical precedents, not as the current statutory citation.
